statement: A role in `models/registry.yaml` shall name exactly one of `family` or `model`, where a family resolves to the family's newest member as the default (as in AD-035-R2) and a model id is used exactly, neither form is privileged and both are lines of configuration in `models/registry.yaml`, and the registry shall refuse a role that names both or neither.

The registry shall carry a `models:` catalog keyed by Anthropic model id, with one parameter profile per model declaring its `family` and its `supported_params` (for example `effort: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]`, or `effort: []` when the model takes none), including entries for family heads; `load_registry` shall refuse any catalog id not prefixed `claude-<family>-*`, so that a non-Anthropic id cannot enter before its own task decides how it should work. When `seldon models refresh` runs, it shall probe each model a role names with `--model <id>` and record under the lock's `models:` the served id, `available`, and the evidence file, treating the model as `available: false` with the reason unless the served id equals the requested id exactly. If a model probe fails, then `seldon models refresh` shall not fail the family probes and shall not block writing the lock, and the day's cache shall not cover a named model the lock has never probed.

The registry shall check each role's declared parameters against its model's `supported_params` at load, and shall refuse at load, naming the role, the parameter and the model, any parameter the model does not support or any value it does not take, because a parameter must never be silently dropped at launch. The launcher shall pass exactly the declared, supported parameters, so a model whose profile is `effort: []` launches with no `--effort` flag and no `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`, while AD-036-R8 holds for every model whose profile has effort levels, the role naming one. A family role shall be checked at load against the head the documented-default table was read for, and checked again at resolution against the head the lock serves when the catalog has that head; a bump to a head with no profile shall be named `profile_missing` in the `models_lock_bumped` event.

If the model named by a role is unavailable, then the role resolver shall fail the role as `model_unavailable` and shall never fall back to another model, because that is the substitution R6 exists to stop. R5 shall accept the family heads plus every named model the lock marks available, and shall refuse a `**Model:** <role>` header naming an unavailable model, quoting the lock. The four `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` variables shall still carry the family heads, `--model` shall carry the named id, and the R6 receipt shall compare the served id with that named id. AD-037's checker over a role naming a model shall map by that model's catalog family (an opus model is read by fable), and a calibration report shall stay per judge id over generator id; AD-037 governs both, nothing in it changes, and the base task's R13 is not a ruling here.
